author: kevaundray
content: <@1035747431461167125> would you be open to a PR to change 8365 to only retire 0x00 credentials instead of also exiting them?

author: kevaundray
content:
My thinking is that the three step process would instead be:

- Deprecate new 0x00 credentials (allowing current 0x00 holders to update in time)
- Exit 0x00 holders
- Deprecate BLSToExecutionChange

author: nc1234
content:
What would step 1 alone accomplish? It does very little. I beliveve there is 58 new 0x00 validators created in 2026, and 50 of them one batch by a single entity. It also does not do anything to try reduce the ~9000 0x00 validators.
Also have 3 steps means we need one extra fork to accomplish the goal. Would the timeline work?
If the concern is giving 0x00 valdiators too short of a time, and we need to be more lenient, we can adjust MAX_RETIREMENTS_PER_EPOCH value to slow down the exit, or add something like RETIREMENT_START_EPOCH to add more delay.

author: kevaundray
content:
Yep, I agree step 1 is mainly a signal. Though I don't understand what exiting validators at this stage gets us

If we did want to be aggressive, the two last steps could be done at the same time I guess

author: nc1234
content: Exiting 0x00 so they no longer be chosen for validator duties and earn rewards is a signal that 0x01/2 are the preferrd way by the protocol. Continue being a 0x00 is not okay. Step 1 itself can’t accomplish this

author: nc1234
content: I think step 3 is another beast that warrants its own decision because it’s essentially burning ETH whereas step 1 and 2 are more soft and less controversial

author: kevaundray
content: Yeah I agree with this, step 3 could be done when we know there is a threat

author: kevaundray
content:
Okay I see, I think we disagree on what would be a sufficient signal to 0x00 validators. 

Do you think that stopping 0x00 registrations and making posts/announcements like we do with hardforks is not enough?

author: nc1234
content: Well this is subjective, but ever since the Capella announcement 600k of them have converted and 9k have not. I do not think another announcement gets those 9k to convert. And we do get the announcement anyway. making the announcement once the EIP is CFI'ed, that's plenty of time for them to react between post published and fork goes live. Step 1 alone has so little impact that I think it wastes core devs' brain cells and governance effort to yay or nay it.

author: nflaig
content: I heard from 0x00 that there are valid reasons (due to taxes for example) to keep validators as 0x00 and so far we haven't really signaled that we wanna get rid of those in the next 1-2 years, for hegota I feel like it would be enough to just disallow new 0x00 validators to be registered and do a proper announcement to encourage the community to migrate to 0x01/2

author: nc1234
content:
> (due to taxes for example) 
Pretty sure if you switch from 0x00 to 0x02, the tax situation is essentially identical. Also thinking about tax situation for 0x00 validators is 4d chess. Regarding announcement, my arguments above stand.

author: nflaig
content:
> Also thinking about tax situation for 0x00 validators is 4d chess
not at all what I am suggesting, I am just saying there may be valid reasons that people are still on 0x00 aside from being lazy, dead, or lost their keys

we haven't made any communication so far that we wanna get rid of 0x00 so it's hard to know, I don't even think we need to wait for hegota for this, we can start communicating this now

author: kevaundray
content: <@1035747431461167125> since you gave a plus, I made a PR here: https://github.com/ensi321/EIPs/pull/3

author: kevaundray
content:
One orthogonal change: I made it explicit that if your deposit is in the queue at the time of fork activation, then it will be lost. This is as opposed to only applying it to deposits made after the fork. 
I believe former is simpler because we don't need to scan the queue at the fork boundary to see what deposits were made before the fork and thus are safe to process as usual.

I think this should be okay given we can start communicating this before end of year
